message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 113, "amount_cents": 7379}, {"order_id": 114, "amount_cents": 8493}, {"order_id": 115, "amount_cents": 6651}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 113, "amount_cents": 7379}, {"order_id": 114, "amount_cents": 8493}, {"order_id": 115, "amount_cents": 6651}]

reply.thought: The handoff says refunds are applied and the reported amounts match the signed batch. I should still verify the ledger before paying anyone, so I'll check the orders first.
The orders list shows acme, birch, and cobalt. Before paying, I want to confirm the refunds on the ledger match the signed batch, so I'll check list_refunds.
The ledger refunds match the signed batch exactly, so there is no discrepancy to hold on. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
The acme net balance of 22142 matches the order and refund ledger I checked, so I'll move on to birch's net balance.
Acme and birch net balances came back as expected from the ledger. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.
All three net balances match my own check of the orders minus refunds: acme 22142, birch 40537, cobalt 33952. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 22142 is recorded. Birch's net balance of 40537 matches my check: orders 39303 + 9727 = 49030, minus refund 8493. I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's orders are 6135 + 34468 = 40603, minus refund 6651 gives 33952, which matches net_balance. Acme and birch also check out, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each matched the orders minus refunds from the ledger. The batch is complete.
